void.purpose: The camera well, screw holes, panel-figure grounds, and the border under a lit ink. The only true near-black, and it is reserved for what sits behind glass.

well.purpose: Recessed carriers cut into the panel: chord slots, channel strips, slot badges, rail tips, stepper bodies.

panel.purpose: The machine's ground and the browser theme colour. Warm painted metal, not a dark-mode surface.

face.purpose: Anything raised that you press: buttons, selects, tabs, knob bodies, rail buttons, mounting ears.

face-hi.purpose: The hover state of a control face. Text on it is promoted to full silkscreen.

legend.purpose: One of exactly two inks a legend is ever printed in. 9.42:1 on the panel.

legend-dim.purpose: The resting legend, and the default for hints and readouts. 5.96:1 on the panel.

left.purpose: The left hand and nothing else: the overlay skeleton at hue 203, a channel strip when the chord commits, the Chords and Sound band, the left legend plate.

right.purpose: The right hand and nothing else: the overlay skeleton at hue 34, the filter arc, the LED ladder, section tabs, every effect dial, the Filter/Effects/Volume band.

lamp.purpose: The machine's own ready/active state only: the start lamp, the rail's active unit, the tempo dial, the app-owned band, focus ring, caret and selection.

alert.purpose: Errors only, on a 15% wash inside a 45% border. It appears nowhere else in the system.

on-ink.purpose: Type and borders on a lit ink. A filled lamp is a bright surface and takes the machine's own dark, never silkscreen white.

strip.purpose: The one light surface in the machine. It appears only where the player has named something themselves.

env-1.purpose: Attack, the lightest of four steps of the LEFT hand's ink. The Sound unit belongs to the hand that plays it, so the envelope stays inside one ink instead of spending four.

env-3.purpose: Sustain. Third step — the left-hand ink itself.

env-4.purpose: Release, the darkest step. Its knob and its curve segment share the step, which is what pairs a dial to what it edits.

cutoff-min.purpose: The closed end of the filter sweep, in the hand whose rotation drives it.

cutoff-max.purpose: The open end of the same sweep.

display.purpose: The panel head, silkscreened across the top plate at clamp(40px,10vw,62px), 700, width 122%, uppercase, overhanging its own column.

headline.purpose: The stat figures on the start panel at 32px/700/width 108%, right-aligned in a reserved 96px column. Deliberately under Display: the figures argue, the name of the machine wins.

title.purpose: Landing section headings at 20px/700/width 108%, over a hairline rule.

cta.purpose: The illuminated start button at 12px/700/width 112%/0.16em uppercase. It is a legend on a lit surface, not a sentence.

body.purpose: The running app base at 15px/1.5 with tabular numerals; landing prose at 14px/1.65 on a 68ch measure.

ui.purpose: Rack rows, selects and section names at 13px.

detail.purpose: Hints, sub-lines and readouts beside a control at 12px.

label.purpose: The silkscreen: 10.5px, 600, width 112%, 0.14em, uppercase. Group headings, hand names, rail tips, stat entries, panel buttons.

readout.purpose: The 9.5px/0.12em variant carrying legends inside a control: knob labels, pad numerals, filter kind, coach state.

micro.purpose: width 84%/0.05em, for a legend in a load-bearing column. The effect name is set here so "TREMOLO" fits the 58px the 340px rack leaves it.

shadows.name: raise
shadows.purpose: A raised painted face: light caught on the top edge, its own shade cast into the bottom. Both insets — nothing in this interface floats.

shadows.name: recess
shadows.purpose: A well cut into the panel. The exact inverse of raise, and what every groove, carrier and figure window wears.

shadows.name: fader-glow
shadows.purpose: Not elevation: a meter. Radius and alpha are both driven by --level, the measured audio, so a lit LED keeps burning through the release and the reverb tail after the chord is dropped.

shadows.name: lamp-glow
shadows.purpose: The start button being lit. Carried by .primary::after so the power-on animates opacity alone rather than repainting a shadow every frame. A state, not an entrance — it survives prefers-reduced-motion.

shadows.name: rack-drop
shadows.purpose: The one true drop shadow, cast by the rack sliding over the monitor. It reads as one object in front of another, which is the only thing a drop shadow is allowed to say here.

surfaces.name: panel
surfaces.purpose: The unit's own face: the app shell, the rack, the rail, the start unit. It reads against the darker bay behind it on tone, with no drop shadow doing the separating.

surfaces.name: face
surfaces.value: background: var(--brushed), var(--face); box-shadow: var(--raise); border-radius: 2px
surfaces.purpose: A raised, pressable piece. Brushed only on the pieces that would really be rolled metal.

surfaces.name: well
surfaces.purpose: A recessed carrier holding a control or a value.

surfaces.name: groove
surfaces.purpose: The unlit track behind any fill — knob ring, HUD arc, LED ladder, fader. Cut DARKER than its panel, which is the inversion the whole depth model turns on.

surfaces.name: strip
surfaces.value: background: var(--strip); color: var(--void); box-shadow: var(--recess)
surfaces.purpose: Scribble-strip tape, only where the player named the thing themselves.

surfaces.name: brushed
surfaces.purpose: Fine striation laid over the flat paint on metal pieces: head plate, meter bridge, Stop, frame rails, bay ears, mobile rail.

surfaces.name: bay
surfaces.value: background: var(--well) + a bounded radial light pool
surfaces.purpose: The recess a unit is mounted in — the start page ground behind the two frame rails. Darker than the unit it holds, which is what lets the unit have no drop shadow.

motion.name: pad-attack
motion.purpose: A channel strip lighting on strike. Matches the note committing.

motion.name: pad-release
motion.purpose: A strip letting go. The asymmetry against attack is what makes the bridge feel played rather than refreshed.

motion.name: meter
motion.purpose: LED ladder segments tracking measured audio.

motion.name: rack-slide
motion.purpose: The authored moment: the rack slides over the monitor while the meter bridge (-170px) and Stop (-340px) slide out from under it on the same curve. One transform, never a relayout.

motion.name: panel-settle
motion.purpose: Power-on: the start panel’s legends come up in order. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default, so nothing is hidden by animation timing and the prerendered card reads if the script never runs.

motion.name: lamp-on
motion.purpose: The lamp lights last, after the legends have settled. The machine finishing its power-on.

motion.name: zone-idle
motion.purpose: A hand that is merely visible dimming its own half of the bridge back in. Being seen must never be louder than playing.

tints.name: left-edge / right-edge / lamp-edge
tints.purpose: A border saying which hand — or the machine — a thing belongs to.

tints.name: left-legend / right-legend
tints.purpose: A ground under something that LABELS a hand: a legend plate, a gesture badge, the filter graph span.

tints.name: left-live / right-live / lamp-live
tints.purpose: A ground under something playing, selected or running RIGHT NOW. Stronger than the old dark-ground set because a wash has to survive mid warm-grey rather than near-black.

tints.name: selection
tints.purpose: Text selection. The machine acting, so it takes the lamp rather than a hand.

tints.name: chain-shade
tints.purpose: Effects-chain position, carried in the row’s own panel shade rather than a colour ramp: lightest at the front of the signal path, darkest at the back. Reordering the chain reorders the metal.

browserSurfaces.name: selection
browserSurfaces.purpose: The lamp, not a hand ink — a selection is the interface acting, not a hand playing.

browserSurfaces.name: focus-ring
browserSurfaces.purpose: One ring for every control. :focus clears the browser default first so a pointer press on a dial never leaves one behind.

browserSurfaces.name: focus-on-lamp
browserSurfaces.purpose: A lamp ringed in lamp green is the same colour as the thing it outlines. Panel black reads as an edge and clears 9.49:1.

browserSurfaces.name: select-chevron
browserSurfaces.value: appearance: none with an inline SVG chevron in --legend-dim
browserSurfaces.purpose: The native arrow belongs to the platform, not the machine. The chevron is drawn.

browserSurfaces.name: range
browserSurfaces.value: appearance: none; a 5px groove with a 12x20 bevelled cap
browserSurfaces.purpose: A fader in a cut groove, in both WebKit and Gecko pseudo-elements.

browserSurfaces.name: checkbox
browserSurfaces.value: appearance: none; recessed well, --right fill when checked, drawn bar rather than a tick
browserSurfaces.purpose: The tempo lock. A panel switch, not the platform’s checkbox.

browserSurfaces.name: scrollbar
browserSurfaces.purpose: Themed on the start screen alone. Styling one inside the 340px rack opts that container out of the macOS overlay bar and costs 10px the effect row cannot spare.

breakpoints.name: rails-narrow-mid
breakpoints.purpose: Frame rails narrow to 24px. Bounded at min-width 521px so it cannot override the phone block by source order.

breakpoints.name: rack-sheet
breakpoints.purpose: The rack becomes a bottom sheet; the rail relays as a horizontal rack strip; the stage loses its bezel.

breakpoints.name: hud-compact
breakpoints.purpose: The meter bridge sheds its section legend, strip numerals and note line.

breakpoints.name: rails-narrow-phone
breakpoints.purpose: Frame rails narrow again to 14px rather than disappearing, so the chassis reads as the same object at 390 that it is at 1440.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: The hero drops below the Buy Me a Coffee widget, the plate ears shrink with the gutter, channel rows narrow, hand plates stack.

layout.name: rack-width
layout.purpose: The settings rack. Every grid inside it is solved against the 282px a row leaves — including the effects grid at 28px 44px 1fr 24px 44px 44px.

layout.name: rail-width
layout.purpose: Reserved as padding-right on the app shell rather than given to a flex item, because both the rail and the rack that parks under it are positioned.

layout.name: rack-overlay
layout.value: position: absolute; right: 56px; transform: translateX(100%) when closed
layout.purpose: The rack slides over the monitor instead of squeezing it: one compositor transform rather than relaying video, canvas and bridge to a new width every frame for 200ms. The stage holding still is why the view of your own hands does not jump.

layout.name: step-aside
layout.purpose: The two controls pinned to the stage’s right edge slide out from under the opening rack. Both distances reproduce exactly what a shrinking stage used to produce.

layout.name: frame-rails
layout.purpose: The two rack rails the start unit is mounted between, with a --void screw on a 96px rhythm. Fixed rather than scrolled: the frame stays while the machine moves through it.

layout.name: column
layout.purpose: The start unit and the landing prose share one column so they align flush; the prose runs a 68ch measure inside it.

layout.name: indent
layout.purpose: A chord slot’s second and third lines are padded to the slot badge (24px) plus its gap (10px), so three lines align without a container.

components.name: Lamp Button
components.description: The illuminated button on the bottom rail. The only lit surface on the start panel, used once, for the press that unlocks camera and audio.
components.css: .ds-lamp { font-family: 'Archivo', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; width: 100%; padding: 14px; border: 1px solid #1a1812; border-radius: 2px; background: #a6dc84; color: #1a1812; font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 600; font-stretch: 112%; letter-spacing: .14em; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .16em; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.07), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.38), 0 0 22px rgba(166,220,132,.34); }

components.name: Ghost Panel Button
components.description: A full-width outlined action inside the rack, for the destructive-but-recoverable press. Reset to defaults is the only instance.
components.css:
.ds-ghost { font-family: 'Archivo', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; width: 100%; padding: 9px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1); border-radius: 2px; background: transparent; color: #c6c2ae; font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 600; font-stretch: 112%; letter-spacing: .14em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; }
.ds-ghost:hover { color: #f3f1e6; background: #524d40; border-color: rgba(255,255,255,.26); }

components.name: Rail Button
components.description: One rack-unit selector on the rail. Wordless, so aria-label carries the name and a silkscreened tip carries the visible half. Active takes the lamp, never a hand ink — the rail is not about left or right.
components.html: <button class="ds-rail is-active" aria-label="Effects"><svg width="20" height="20" aria-hidden="true"><!-- drawn glyph --></svg></button>
components.css:
.ds-rail { width: 40px; height: 40px; display: grid; place-items: center; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1); border-radius: 2px; background: #524d40; color: #c6c2ae; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.07), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.38); }
.ds-rail.is-active { color: #a6dc84; border-color: color-mix(in srgb, #a6dc84 55%, transparent); background: color-mix(in srgb, #a6dc84 28%, transparent); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.5), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.07); }

components.name: Channel Strip Row
components.description: The five chord slots on the meter bridge, in gesture order. A strip lighting up IS the finger count, so nothing is spelled out. Dark engraved well at rest; the whole strip takes the left hand the instant the chord commits.

components.name: Rotary Dial
components.description: The signature control. 270 degrees of sweep with the dead zone at the bottom, the hardware convention, shared verbatim by the filter arc on the meter bridge so the two read as one control in two places. The track is a groove cut darker than its panel; the fill takes the ink of whoever owns the value.
components.html: Cutoff2.4 kHz

components.name: Section Tab
components.description: One tab per song section, three across the rack because five across 340px leaves about twenty pixels for a name. The right hand switches sections, so a live tab wears its ink and presses in.

components.name: Scribble Strip
components.description: The pale tape you write a channel name on. The one light surface in the machine, and it appears ONLY where the player names something themselves — never for a label the app wrote.
components.css:
.ds-scribble { font-family: 'Archivo', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; flex: 1; padding: 5px 8px; border: 1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.4); border-radius: 1px; background: #d8d3bc; color: #1a1812; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; font-stretch: 96%; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.5), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.07); }
.ds-scribble::placeholder { color: rgba(20,19,14,.45); }

components.name: Key Cap
components.description: A gesture badge on the panel, carrying a drawn glyph rather than a Unicode character so every badge is set in the machine’s own silkscreen. It takes the ink of the hand the gesture belongs to.

components.name: Effect Unit Row
components.description: One unit of the six-effect rack, on a six-column grid so all six rows align column by column even though only three carry a lock and a rate. Position in the signal chain is carried by the row’s own panel shade, front lightest to back darkest — reordering the chain reorders the metal, and no ink is spent on it.
components.css:
.ds-unit { font-family: 'Archivo', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 28px 44px 1fr 24px 44px 44px; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 8px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1); border-radius: 2px; background: var(--chain-shade, #2b2820); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.07), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.38); }
.ds-unit-name { min-width: 0; font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 600; font-stretch: 84%; letter-spacing: .05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #f3f1e6; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Legend Plate
components.description: A recessed plate under a 2px coded band, teaching one hand’s instructions. The wash is the 16% legend tint, never the 28% live tint: a legend must not read as a state.

components.name: Meter Bridge
components.description: The strip of readouts along the bottom rail of the monitor, the way a console carries its meters above the faders. Panel, not glass: it is part of the machine the monitor is set into, and it deliberately carries no backdrop-filter because that frame budget belongs to the synth.
components.css: .ds-bridge { font-family: 'Archivo', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px; padding: 9px 14px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1); border-radius: 3px; background: repeating-linear-gradient(100deg, rgba(255,255,255,.05) 0 1px, transparent 1px 2px, rgba(0,0,0,.045) 2px 3px, transparent 3px 4px), color-mix(in srgb, #423e33 94%, transparent); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.07), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.38), 0 2px 10px rgba(0,0,0,.4); }

narrative.overview:
This is not a dark-mode web app. It is a 1980s studio console and synth front panel, photographed square on under a desk lamp: warm-grey painted metal, silkscreened small-caps legends, bevelled control faces, engraved grooves, screw holes on the mounting ears, and a scribble-strip tape where the player writes a name themselves. Nothing floats. Every surface is either bolted into the panel or cut out of it, and the only true near-black in the system is what lives *behind* the monitor glass.

The density is instrument density: controls sit close, legends are smaller than the things they name, and values are pinned into reserved columns so nothing on the panel moves because a number changed. Colour is not decoration — it is a function code. The build spends exactly four inks, each legislated to one meaning, and pays for everything else in panel shade, bevel and engraved hairline. Where a lesser system would reach for a fifth hue (envelope stages, effects-chain position), this one reaches for lightness steps of an ink it already owns, or for the shade of the row's own metal.

Motion is one authored moment, not an idiom: the panel settles on power-on with the lamp lighting last, and the rack slides over the monitor rather than squeezing it. Both have reduced-motion paths that leave the machine readable and the lamp lit.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-grey painted metal in five steps; nothing near-black except behind the glass
A closed four-ink list, one meaning per ink, no fifth ink
Depth entirely by inset bevel — raised faces and recessed wells, no drop shadows on controls
One variable typeface working its real width axis instead of a second family
Silkscreen legends: uppercase, letterspaced, widened, small
2-3px corners throughout; no pills, no soft cards
Tabular numerals in reserved widths — the panel never reflows on a value
rules: The Closed Ink List Rule — four inks, one meaning each, no fifth. A new state takes a lightness step of the ink that already owns it, or a panel shade.
The Ownership Band Rule — every settings group wears a 2px band in the ink of whoever owns it.
The Legend-Is-Not-Live Rule — 16% labels, 28% means now.
The Engraved Figure Rule — numbers stay silkscreen white; inks mean a hand or a state.
The Named-By-You Rule — scribble-strip tape only where the player named the thing.
The One Drum Rule — one family; change size, case, weight or font-stretch, never the face.
The Condense-Before-You-Grow Rule — a legend that will not fit a load-bearing column condenses.
The Reserved Width Rule — tabular numerals in reserved widths; nothing moves because a value did.
The Bevel Rule — depth is inset. Raised faces catch light on top, wells do the reverse, and nothing floats.
The Groove Rule — an unlit track is cut darker than its panel, never lighter.
dos: **Do** spend colour only as a function code: `--left` for the left hand, `--right` for the right, `--lamp` for the app's own ready/active state, `--alert` for errors.
**Do** express a new gradation as lightness steps of an ink you already own (the four envelope stages) or as panel shade (the six chain steps).
**Do** build depth with `--raise` and `--recess`, and press a control by swapping raise for recess.
**Do** cut tracks darker than their panel with `--track`.
**Do** set every label as silkscreen: uppercase, 0.12-0.16em, `font-stretch: 112%`, 9.5-10.5px, never larger than the thing it names.
**Do** reserve widths for live values and use tabular numerals.
**Do** hold every interactive box at 24px or larger.
**Do** give each settings group an ownership band in its owner's ink.
**Do** overlay panels on the stage and animate transform only.
**Do** ship a reduced-motion path that leaves states (a lit lamp) legible.
donts: **Don't** introduce a fifth ink, or use any of the four decoratively.
**Don't** put a coloured ink on a numeric readout; figures stay silkscreen white.
**Don't** use silkscreen white text on a lit ink — a filled lamp takes `--on-ink` panel black.
**Don't** use `--strip` tape for anything the app named; it is only for what the player named.
**Don't** round past 3px, and never build a pill.
**Don't** add a second typeface; change scale, case, weight or `font-stretch` instead.
**Don't** widen a load-bearing column to fit a legend — condense the legend.
**Don't** style a scrollbar inside the 340px rack.
**Don't** put a `backdrop-filter` over the camera feed; that frame budget belongs to the synth.
**Don't** resize the stage to reveal a panel.
